question:
**A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.**

Rita said, "Alas! I am ruined."

options.text: Rita exclaimed with sorrow that she was ruined.
Rita exclaimed sadly that I am ruined.

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Rita exclaimed with sorrow that she was ruined.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **direct speech**, and the task is to convert it into **indirect speech.**
 
• In the direct speech, the phrase **"Alas!"** is an expression of sorrow, so it must be conveyed as "exclaimed with sorrow" in the indirect speech.
 
• The pronoun "I" in the direct speech is changed to "she" in the indirect speech to match the subject "Rita."
 
• The tense in the indirect speech follows the rule of **sequence of tenses**, so "am" is changed to "was."

Correct sentence: *Rita exclaimed with sorrow that she was ruined.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• While converting from direct to indirect speech, expressions of emotions like "Alas!" (sorrow) or "Hurrah!" (joy) are replaced by phrases such as "exclaimed with sorrow" or "exclaimed with joy."
 
• Pronouns in direct speech are adjusted to match the subject of the reporting verb in indirect speech.
 
• The tense of the verb is typically shifted back in time (present to past) in indirect speech.
 
• Option 1 and 3 fail to capture the emotional tone of "Alas!" while Option 4 incorrectly uses "I" instead of "she."
